findings.text: follow-on: anchor eligibility for a sibling is now decided by families.is_placeholder_description (families.py:472), which tests `not description or description == PLACEHOLDER` without stripping whitespace, while the description returned for that same member is normalised by the local _real (context.py:858), which strips and blanks the placeholder. A whitespace-only description ("   ") was excluded by the retired inline filter (old code kept only rows with a truthy _real(description)) but is now eligible as the anchor and renders as an empty string. Reachability is marginal, but the change leaves two predicates for one notion of a real description in one call path; a single owner would close it.

Both scores below full because the fetch_sibling_family-vs-select_anchor equality is anchored to a literal only through its third conjunct: the first two terms are two calls to the same function and move together, so they carry no independent signal on their own. I confirmed the named test passes at head by re-running it (reviewer_spotcheck.log, 1 passed, EXIT=0).

The done-when's rg check returns nothing at head (`grep -n 'coalesce(c.{seg}'` on the head blob is exit 1) and build_worklist calls _invariant_projection("c") at harmonize.py:403. Held below full because the after_suite revision field names the base sha rather than the head commit whose content it gated (the log header carries tree-dirty-yes), so the record alone does not pin the head revision.
justifications.fit: The added names follow the surrounding idiom and carry no forbidden label. DOCS_STAGE_ACCEPTED, is_placeholder_description and select_anchor are mechanism names with docstrings, matching families.py's existing PATTERN_* / _invariant_projection style (all-caps module constants, lower_snake functions). select_anchor is imported into harmonize and re-exported through __all__ (harmonize.py:637), preserving the public surface. No plan, sprint, gate or ticket label and no author attribution appears in any added symbol, comment, docstring, test name or filename; the fragment's element ids derive from the node's own mechanism name, which is the landing-record convention.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The brief names four defects to clear and the diff clears each: the two anchor rules collapse into one owner (families.select_anchor) called by both fetch_sibling_family (context.py:896) and the harmonize paths, with the tie now broken by id; the fetch_sibling_family docstring's invariant set and variation axes are corrected against PATTERN_INVARIANT_SEGMENTS/PATTERN_VARIATION_AXES (context.py:778-802); build_worklist reuses _invariant_projection; and the members-query test is replaced with one that pins an independent literal. I verified the docstring's stated segments against families.py:421-449 and they match exactly, with no scope creep beyond the four defects, over the six declared paths.
justifications.reuse: The change is a consolidation, not a fork. It moves select_anchor from harmonize.py into families.py, the module that already owns PATTERN_INVARIANT_SEGMENTS, PATTERN_VARIATION_AXES and _invariant_projection, and both callers now extend that owner rather than carrying their own copy; the inline anchor selection that context.py previously implemented is deleted in the same commit, and build_worklist stops restating the invariant column list beside _invariant_projection. I searched the repository for other owners of these capabilities: no pre-existing generic anchor-selection or invariant-projection helper exists outside families.py, and the moved code is the same logic, so no second implementation is introduced. The single residual duplication is the placeholder predicate (context._real vs families.is_placeholder_description), recorded as a follow-on finding.
justifications.scope_discipline: Commit-by-commit the diff is confined to the six declared files: c1468c04e edits the three production modules and the two test files, fda647599 adds only the landing fragment. The three production edits are each one of the four brief defects (anchor unification, docstring, projection reuse, test replacement), with no unrelated refactor — the _DOCS_STAGE_ACCEPTED -> DOCS_STAGE_ACCEPTED renames are direct consequences of the move, and harmonize.py:424 still uses the retained PATTERN_INVARIANT_SEGMENTS import so no dead import is left. The granted figures directory is unused and no plan or index file is touched; the reviewed worktree is clean at head with only the expected untracked .venv.
